Article Title: UPI MDR will fund innovation, protect small merchants: NPCI’s Dilip Asbe
Article Text:
The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed.

Why this sudden move to charge MDR on UPI, and how did you decide on the Rs 2,000 threshold and the 0.4% MDR? Will you review the scheme periodically?

How much is expected to be collected in the first year, around Rs 15,000 crore?

What is the rationale for the charge given that the government can easily foot a bill of Rs 20,000 crore, as it is a tiny fraction of its budget, especially when it spends thousands of crores on non-merit subsidies? Why can't banks, NPCI or RBI bear the burden?

What is being done to ensure that customers are not burdened with MDR? Also, is NPCI proposing a relook at GST?

How do you propose to utilise the money to develop the market? Do you see banks and other service providers offering loyalty points for UPI transactions, as is the case with credit cards?

Will there be a check on merchants and consumers splitting transactions to avoid MDR over Rs 2,000?

The new system has created confusion around several aspects of the scheme...

How do you respond to allegations that the decision was taken under US pressure?

Why is the P2PM limit so low?

The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed. In an interview with TOI, Dilip Asbe, MD & CEO, explains how the new fee structure protects small transactions while charging larger merchants, who already pay fees on card payments. Besides, there are a host of exemptions aimed at shielding consumers and small merchants. NPCI expects Rs 13,000-15,000 crore in the first year, with 5% of this being ploughed back to support small merchants, while periodic reviews will assess the model.UPI P2M was charged from inception, and we followed the global model of keeping P2P free and P2M at reasonable cost recovery, much lower than the prescribed MDR for debit and credit cards, net banking or wallets. The government's decision on zero MDR in 2020 helped UPI expand rapidly among merchants during the Covid period. In the last four years, the UPI ecosystem — namely NPCI, banks, fintech start-ups and industry bodies such as the Payments Council of India and IBA — has been seeking a review to ensure a self-sustainable system that can create long-term value for the country, citizens and merchants. UPI growth has slowed, and India remains under-penetrated compared with China and Brazil, where almost 90% of the adult population uses digital payments every day, versus 40% in our case.So, we need investment to expand digital payments, especially among the poor.The charges were finalised primarily keeping in mind the costs incurred by various players to process UPI transactions. Instead of a fixed-fee model, which would penalise low-ticket transactions, we opted for percentage-based charges so that high-ticket transactions with margins can contribute the majority of the MDR. Certain categories with high ticket sizes but lower margins were kept at a flat Rs 5 irrespective of the ticket size, to continue driving adoption. If you review the rates, they are almost at par with global rates for QR-based payments, which are charged similarly without making any exceptions, while these charges remain much lower than those for debit or credit card transactions currently paid by large merchants.It may take some time for the system to settle down. Maybe, in the first year, we will collect Rs 13,000-15,000 crore, of which 5% will be allocated to the small merchant fund to incentivise digital-payment growth among small merchants. We will soon release the guidelines on this.The idea is not to burden small players, as we expect over 80% of the MDR charges to come from businesses with over Rs 1,000 crore turnover. Most of them are already accepting cards and paying much higher MDR on cards under the current construct. There are competing demands on public funds, and this is the best way to make the ecosystem sustainable, grow and innovate without depending on subsidies.NPCI is a not-for-profit entity; all its profits are reinvested in creating infrastructure, reserves for settlement guarantees, innovation and resilience. NPCI needs to not only survive but thrive for the next 100 years.Banks continue to make substantial investments in maintaining and scaling the UPI ecosystem, with annual expenditure often exceeding Rs 2,000 crore for most large banks. At the same time, a Rs 5,000 cash withdrawal can often be substituted by 50 to 100 UPI transactions, highlighting the scale and efficiency of digital payments. While the transition from cash to digital payments has undoubtedly delivered savings through lower cash-handling and ATM-servicing costs, banks also incur significant costs in building and operating resilient, secure and scalable UPI payment infrastructure.Over the last six years, the overall ecosystem has invested over Rs 75,000 crore to maintain and grow the UPI ecosystem without much cost recovery. These investments and innovations will benefit the country in the long run.Running the UPI ecosystem requires around Rs 21,000 crore annually, and we have sought to protect small merchants and low-value payments to help smaller firms raise capital and invest. The idea is also to have more players to increase competition. As a result, person-to-person transactions and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000, with no upper cap on cumulative or repeat transactions, all recurring payments or AutoPay, and small individual merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month into their own accounts will not face any MDR. Since most of the MDR will be generated from merchants who already accept card payments, the consumer price is already factored into MDR charges, or else we would have seen merchants offering major discounts for UPI and RuPay debit card transactions over the last six years. We have prohibited platform fees and merchants charging customers. We plan to review it periodically along with the ecosystem. On GST, I have no comments to offer since this decision will be made by the finance ministry and GST Council. However, major large merchants will claim an input tax credit for the GST paid.The objective of these charges is to ensure the ecosystem thrives, becomes self-sustainable, and is able to innovate and create value that, in turn, grows UPI. Today, we observe that payment methods with good cost recovery tend to have better innovation and features. For example, EMIs, rewards and discount offers help grow merchant sales, particularly in categories such as electronics. Once cost recovery starts, the ecosystem will create a major drive to onboard new consumers and merchants, install more sound boxes and increase activity in under-penetrated geographies and categories through digitalisation. Amid evolving times and landscapes, it will also allow the ecosystem to invest proactively in cybersecurity and resilience.Any policy that has a ceiling or a floor has these second-order effects. If the consumer is ready to participate in splitting the transactions based on a merchant's request, we do not foresee any harm in this and, accordingly, no upper cap on such transactions has been defined. We believe this may, at best, be a short-term phenomenon and that consumer experience will ultimately win in the long run. What we have seen globally and in India is that it is primarily the consumer's choice that drives digital payments.Yes, but we are working with industry bodies and ecosystem participants to provide clarity. For example, some people have interpreted the no-MDR limit below Rs 2,000 as a daily cap and not a per-transaction limit, which is not the case.The USTR has a reference to a UPI market-share cap of 30%, as well as NCMC standards access to other competing international schemes, which is a fair and factual point, and we believe it must be a country's prerogative to make that decision. We didn't find any reference to charges or MDR, and, as I said above, it benefits competing companies to keep it free.This is more like an intermediate step for a merchant moving from receiving money via standard P2P to graduating into a proper P2M merchant so that it gets the support of a sound box, POS machine or other ancillary services. Even when P2PM merchants move to a proper merchant, they continue to receive transactions up to Rs 2,000 without any charges or cap.
Article Summary: Dilip asbe, md & ceo, npci explains how the new fee structure protects small transactions while charging larger merchants, who already pay fees on card payments. Npci expects rs 13,000-15,000 crore in the first year, with 5% of this being ploughed back to support small merchants.

Article Title: Fortis investors flag legal overhang after Delhi HC order
Article Text:
Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, could create a reputational overhang and weigh on investor confidence.

Domestic and foreign institutional investors of Fortis Healthcare (Fortis) have expressed concern that the Delhi High Court ’s order seeking a forensic audit of transactions involving its former promoters, Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh, could create a reputational overhang and weigh on investor confidence.The Aug 31 high court order came in a case arising from Japanese firm Daiichi Sankyo’s efforts to enforce its arbitral award against the erstwhile Fortis promoters. Last week, Fortis filed a special leave petition (SLP) in the Supreme Court challenging the order.Together, domestic and foreign institutional investors hold over half -- 57% shareholding, while the retail share is over 11% in the company.``The question for the market is whether a transaction that has cleared the entire approval architecture — board, shareholders, CCI, SEBI, the Takeover Code, ever becomes settled’’, Shriram Subramanian MD and founder of InGovern, a proxy advisory firm, told TOI.In 2018, Malaysia's IHH Healthcare acquired a controlling 31.1% stake in Fortis for approximately Rs 4,000 crore.``Questioning a transaction long cleared by all regulators and seeking its forensic audit after nearly a decade, will open a can of worms’’, he added.IHH is a credible strategic investor, and Fortis, after years of promoter-related turmoil and uncertainty, is now on a more stable footing, investors feel, and prolonged legal proceedings could create uncertainty.While the court has made clear that the forensic audit is a fact-finding exercise and does not, by itself, impose liability, investors said the process could still have wider implications for the company.``Capital is mobile and investors have alternatives; prolonged uncertainty can therefore have consequences for the company and its shareholders’’, InGovern said in a note, shared with TOI.The acquisition was approved by the board, cleared by the CCI, and completed under the SEBI Takeover Regulations through an open offer SEBI itself permitted. Neither IHH nor Fortis was a party to the arbitration, the award or the execution proceedings.Investors are also concerned about the possibility of the company being drawn into the matter at a later stage, including through the doctrine of “reverse veil piercing”.The company has also challenged this in its special leave petition arguing that reverse piercing, under which a company’s assets could potentially be subjected to the personal debts or obligations of its (erstwhile) controlling shareholder, has not been recognised by Indian courts.
Article Summary: Malvinder and shivinder mohan singh, could create a reputational overhang and weigh on investor confidence. Last week, fortis filed a special leave petition (slp) in the supreme court challenging the order. Malaysia's ihh healthcare acquired a controlling 31.1% stake in fortis for approximately rs 4,000 crore.

Article Title: Nationwide strike: Banks to remain shut from Monday for three days - what customers need to know
Article Text:
Banks to remain shut for 5 days

What should customers do now?

Here’s what customers could do to avoid disruption:

Complete branch-dependent work beforehand: Customers with requirements that need a branch visit or intervention from bank staff may need to plan them before the proposed strike period.

Why are banks planning a strike?

What has the government said?

Do you have a pending bank visit, payment or other transactions lined up for the month-end? You may want to get it done by Friday!Banking operations across the country are set to face disruption as bank unions have planed a three-day nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With the strike following a weekend holiday, customers could face an effective five-day disruption in banking services.The timing is also significant as September 30 marks the half-yearly closing of banks, when reconciliation, provisioning, and treasury and market operations take place.With banking services likely to face disruption around the end of September, customers may want to plan their banking requirements in advance. Several public sector banks have already advised customers to use digital channels if the strike goes ahead.Services available through digital channels can continue to be accessed through those channels if the strike materialises. The disruption could also affect businesses, government transactions and international banking operations, apart from causing inconvenience to the public.The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), which claims to represent 90 per cent of the banking workforce, has said it will proceed with the strike unless there is a concrete and positive development on its main demand for five-day banking.“Responding to the appeal made by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Indian Banks' Association (IBA), Bank managements to defer the strike, we informed them that if there is any concrete and positive development towards implementation of our demand for introduction of 5 days banking, UFBU will consider the same,” UFBU said in a statement after the meeting with the deputy chief labour commissioner.The statement came after a conciliation meeting on Tuesday remained inconclusive. The union said that in the absence of such a development, it would be constrained to go ahead with the proposed strike on September 28, 29 and 30.The meeting was held a day after the finance ministry appealed to bank employees to refrain from strikes and resolve their remaining demands through dialogue.UFBU's other demands include an update and improvement of pension, a uniform dearness allowance formula for all pensioners and an option for employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS) to move to the old pension scheme (OPS).Bank unions under the UFBU had also gone on a nationwide strike on September 11 over their demands.Representatives of the department of financial services (DFS) and the ministry of finance told the conciliation meeting that the government had been taking several initiatives for the welfare of bank employees. They said five-day banking was also under consideration, but the government would need to take into account the views of various other stakeholders before taking a decision.The representatives therefore asked the UFBU to defer the strike and continue the dialogue.The finance ministry had said that strikes disrupt banking services, inconvenience the public and affect the business of banks. It also said such disruptions ultimately harm the interests of bank employees and that no fruitful outcome is achieved through strikes.The government has assured that it remains committed to the welfare and well-being of bank employees and to addressing their genuine concerns through constructive engagement.
Article Summary: Bank unions have planed a three-day nationwide strike from september 28 to 30. With the strike following a weekend holiday, customers could face an effective five-day disruption in banking services. Several public sector banks have already advised customers to use digital channels if the strike goes ahead.

Article Title: Gold prices surge 60% from Rs 98,000 to Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams in a year; Ganesh Chaturthi sales fall 15% as buyers switch to lighter jewellery, also buy coins
Article Text:
Jewellers remain hopeful that the moderation in demand will prove temporary as the festive calendar progresses.

Gold prices high

Growing interest in coins

Gold hallmarking charges rise

A huge rise in gold prices from the same time last year has led to a drop in gold sales this Ganesh Chaturthi . Gold sales have declined by around 15% year-on-year in volume terms, with consumers either reducing the quantity they bought or opting for lighter jewellery as a sharp increase in gold prices made purchases more expensive, industry executives said.In Mumbai's spot market on Monday, gold was trading at Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams, including 3% goods and services tax. This was around 60% higher than the Rs 98,000 per 10 grams recorded on Ganesh Chaturthi last year, which fell on August 28.“Domestic gold prices have remained at a historic high, which has impacted volume sales. But overall the mood is optimistic, with many people resorting to old gold jewellery exchanges to buy new jewellery, which is mostly lightweight,” said Surendra Mehta, national secretary, India Bullion & Jewellers Association, according to an ET report.Jewellers remain hopeful that the moderation in demand will prove temporary as the festive calendar progresses towards the peak wedding season. Since weddings are also taking place during the festive period, retailers expect buyers to increasingly seek jewellery that can serve multiple purposes, from celebrations and gifting to regular wear.“We are seeing greater interest in diamonds as buyers seek jewellery that is versatile enough for celebrations, gifting and everyday wear,” said Rohan Hemdev, director, Ananya Jewels.Kumar Jain, owner of Umedmal Tilokchand Zaveri, a 100-year-old outlet in Mumbai's Zaveri Bazaar, said demand for bullion in the form of coins and bars had picked up during this year's Ganesh Chaturthi, although volumes remained below last year's level.“Bullion sales in the form of coins and bars have shown traction this Ganesh Chaturthi, even though the volume is lesser than last year.”The increased preference for coins and bars suggests that consumers are still setting aside money for gold during auspicious occasions, but the elevated price of jewellery is making them more cautious about their purchases.The trend also reflects the broader conditions in India's gold market. According to the World Gold Council, the festive season began on a cautious note as the sharp rise in gold prices prompted consumers to adopt a wait-and-watch approach and defer discretionary purchases.Wedding-related demand, however, has remained comparatively resilient, while physical investment demand has stayed steady.There is also growing interest among younger consumers in purchasing jewellery for themselves. Women, in particular, are increasingly buying jewellery to celebrate festivals as well as personal milestones.Hemdev expects festive-season sales to register double-digit growth, helped by wedding demand, rising disposable incomes and evolving consumption habits. He also pointed to the growing role of digital platforms, social media, influencers and celebrity collaborations in making jewellery more aspirational and appealing to younger consumers.“With the ongoing festive season, we expect buying interest to gradually pick up, especially as consumers and jewellery retailers prepare for the period,” said Darshan Desai, CEO, Aspect Bullion & Refinery.In the meantime, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has increased the hallmarking fee for gold articles just before the start of the festive season. The charge, which was earlier Rs 45 per gold article, has now been raised to Rs 75. The fee for silver articles, however, remains unchanged at Rs 35.The change was notified through the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, dated September 14, 2026.BIS hallmarking is the system used to certify the purity of precious metal articles under the Bureau of Indian Standards framework. A hallmarked article carries three important identifiers: the BIS logo, the karat or millesimal fineness and a six-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number.Under the amended Schedule IV, jewellers will now be charged Rs 75 for every gold article sent for hallmarking. A minimum charge of Rs 200 will apply to each consignment.There has been no change in the hallmarking fee for silver. Jewellers will continue to pay Rs 35 per silver article to recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs), with a minimum consignment charge of Rs 150.
Article Summary: Gold sales have declined by around 15% year-on-year in volume terms. In mumbai's spot market on monday, gold was trading at rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams. The bureau of indian standards (bis) has increased the hallmarking fee for gold articles. A minimum charge of rs 200 will apply to each consignment.

Article Title: Tom Brady’s $220 million investment pays off big as franchise valuation jumps to $13 billion in just 9 months in the new season
Article Text:
Tom Brady's investments.(Image via Getty Images)

Tom Brady’s investment in the Las Vegas Raiders turns out to be highly successful in the middle of the new season

Tom Brady has set up a $100 million business empire ever since he retired from the league

Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, has turned into a pretty successful entrepreneur ever since he retired from the league. While he has an ongoing 10 year contract with FOX Sports for a whopping $375 million, one of Tom Brady’s investments has skyrocketed, proving it to be a smart investment decision of his.In October 2024, the New England Patriots legend Tom Brady Tom Wagner, the founder of Knighthood Capital Management, became a minority owner in the Las Vegas Raiders with a $220 million investment.Tom Brady and Tom Wagner’s $220 million investment in the team equated to a 10% stake in the Las Vegas Raiders.A few months ago, as per Forbes, it was reported that the valuation of the Las Vegas Raiders has now skyrocketed as the team is now valued at a whopping $13 billion.Interestingly, the Las Vegas Raiders were worth $7.7 billion in just December 2025, marking a 68.83% increase in valuation in just the last nine months.While the 15 time Pro Bowler Tom Brady has not reacted to this news publicly, he has been public about his little involvement with the day to day operations of the Las Vegas Raiders.In many of his interviews, Tom Brady has openly spoken about how he is always available for the team but does not get too involved with how the team operates on a day to day basis.When Tom Brady decided to invest in the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024, it had attracted a lot of criticism as he was still working with FOX Sports then.Luckily, things worked out for the New England Patriots’ legend and Tom Brady was allowed to invest in the team by the NFL.After Tom Brady retired from the league, he has remained passionate about investing aggressively in growing brands and setting up his own businesses.Apart from investing in the Las Vegas Raiders, Tom Brady has also invested in the WNBA’s Las Vegas Aces, and English soccer club Birmingham City.In a recent interview, Tom Brady reflected on it as he said, “I don’t look at it from a business standpoint…I look at it from a purpose driven standpoint. For me, it’s about being a part of competition and trying to help other people be successful, so I enjoy the process and the product that happens on the field… I want to see other people be successful in their life and their sporting career.”The NFL legend added, “I had so many mentors that were a part of my life that allowed me to be successful, and if I can play a role in other people’s life then it’s a very exciting thing for me.”With a $300 million net worth, Tom Brady remains dedicated to his business empire.
Article Summary: Tom brady has set up a $100 million business empire ever since he retired from the league. In october 2024, the new england patriots legend tom wagner, the founder of knighthood capital management, became a minority owner in the las vegas raiders. Tom brady and tom wagner’s $220 million investment in the team equated to a 10% stake.

Article Title: How Naomi Osaka invested in a $3.1 million hair business after one woman turned her personal salon frustration into a 4-location company
Article Text:
How Naomi Osaka invested in a $3.1 million hair business after one woman turned her personal salon frustration into a 4-location company(Getty Images)

How Piersten gaines built Pressed Roots around an overlooked customer

How Naomi Osaka joined a group of high-profile Pressed Roots investors

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Naomi Osaka has invested in several businesses outside tennis, but one of her more unusual bets came in the haircare industry. In 2024, Osaka became an investor in Pressed Roots, a salon company founded by Piersten Gaines for customers with textured hair.The business had already shown signs of traction before Osaka came on board. Pressed Roots had generated $2 million in annual revenue in 2022, followed by $3.5 million in 2023. Gaines then raised $3.1 million from a group that included Osaka, Howard Schultz, Meg Whitman, Slauson & Co. and RevTech Ventures.Gaines came up with the idea while studying at Harvard Business School. She had seen how blowout chains such as Drybar offered customers a standard experience, but she struggled to find something similar for textured hair.“I had a lot of really terrible salon experiences throughout my life,” Gaines told Fortune in 2024. She wanted to build a chain where customers could expect trained stylists and a consistent service each time they visited.Before putting money into a permanent location, Gaines tested the idea through pop-ups in Boston, Atlanta and Dallas. The appointments sold out, giving her evidence that customers would pay for the service.She spent about two years running pop-ups before raising $500,000 to open her first permanent location in Dallas.The first salon was scheduled to open in March 2020. Gaines held a soft launch three days before the planned opening, with more than 250 people attending. She said the salon was already booked for its first month before the pandemic forced it to close.That setback did not change the basic business model. Pressed Roots focused on the silk blowout and built its own stylist training programme. Its stylists also work as employees instead of independent contractors, giving the company more control over the customer experience.The $3.1 million raise came after Gaines had already shown investors that customers were willing to spend on the service. Inc. reported that Pressed Roots generated about $2 million in revenue in 2022 before reaching $3.5 million the following year.Osaka was not the only prominent name attached to the round. Former HP CEO Meg Whitman and former Starbucks CEO Howard Schultz’s Schultz Family Foundation also invested. Slauson & Co. and RevTech Ventures were among the other backers, while Gaines also connected with angel investors through Slauson & Co.The business had a clear pitch beyond the salon itself. Gaines told Fortune that customers in her target demographic continued spending on their hair even during the pandemic. Her argument to investors was that haircare was not simply an occasional luxury for these customers.“Our goal is to make quality haircare accessible,” Gaines told Fortune.In April 2025, Pressed Roots had four locations and about 200 employees. Gaines was also looking beyond the salons, with plans to expand into hair products and accessories. The company’s Houston expansion had already taken its footprint outside the Dallas-Fort Worth area.The investment therefore came after Gaines had spent years testing the idea, building revenue and proving that a specialised salon could attract a loyal customer base. Osaka joined a wider group of investors backing a business that had already moved from a Harvard classroom idea to a growing Texas-based company.
Article Summary: How naomi osaka invested in a $3.1 million hair business after one woman turned her personal salon frustration into a 4-location company. In 2024, osaka became an investor in pressed roots, a salon company founded by piersten gaines for customers with textured hair. The business had already shown signs of traction before osaka came on board.

Article Title: India’s space sovereignty: From building missions to building depth
Article Text:
Tired of too many ads? go ad free now

For decades, the central question was whether India could design, build and launch increasingly complex spacecraft on its own. That question has been answered across multiple fronts, from indigenous launch vehicles and navigation systems to lunar and solar missions, autonomous docking and preparations for human spaceflight.The next question is harder: can India build enough technological, industrial and commercial depth to sustain those capabilities when a critical component is unavailable, a supply chain is disrupted or geopolitical tensions restrict access to foreign technology?That is where the idea of space sovereignty becomes important. Space sovereignty, in practical terms, means having the ability to design, build, launch, operate and protect critical space assets without being vulnerable to a single external supplier, technology or geopolitical pressure.It does not mean producing every component domestically or shutting out international partnerships.Rather, it means retaining control over technologies and infrastructure critical to national security, communications, navigation and strategic decision-making, while having enough domestic capability to replace or rebuild them when access is disrupted.

Article Title: OpenAI expands GPT-6 lineup with cheaper, faster Sol and Luna models
Article Text:
Cheaper models built on the same foundation

How the new models perform

Key features

Availability

OpenAI has released two new models for different needs. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has now introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna models. The company claims that Sol is designed as a high-performance model optimised for complex reasoning, large-scale research and enterprise applications. On the other hand, Luna, is a lighter and more adaptive model which is built for everyday use cases and offer faster responses and lower compute requirements. Both the new models are created with OpenAI’s latest alignment techniques, including safeguards around recursive self-improvement (RSI) and improved oversight mechanisms. OpenAI also stressed on the fact that the launch reflects its commitment to balancing innovation with safety, ensuring that frontier AI systems remain under human control while scaling their capabilities.Earlier this month, OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra, which it describes as the most intelligent and aligned model it has built to date. Sol and Luna extend that same generation of intelligence downward, trained using similar methods as Astra but optimized to advance the frontier on cost efficiency rather than raw capability. OpenAI says the two new models bring Astra's advances in professional work, factuality, coding, computer use, and alignment to faster, more affordable tiers.The economics are the headline change here. Thanks to improvements in caching and inference, OpenAI is cutting API prices for both models by 50% compared to their GPT-5.6 promotional pricing. GPT-6 Sol now costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, down from $4 and $20 respectively. GPT-6 Luna is even cheaper, dropping to $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, down from $0.20 and $1.20. Astra remains OpenAI's top recommendation when uncompromising performance matters most.OpenAI is positioning Sol in particular as a serious contender against rival models at a fraction of the cost. On AutomationBench, a test of real-world business workflows, the company says GPT-6 Sol at its highest effort setting outperforms Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 at max effort while costing just 9% as much per task. On Agents' Last Exam, which evaluates complex, long-horizon professional workflows, Sol scored 56.4% at max effort — ahead of Opus 5's best score in the same evaluation, at 60% lower cost per task.Coding performance also saw a notable jump. On FrontierCode, which grades AI-generated code on whether it's actually ready to merge into real codebases, OpenAI says Sol improved substantially over its GPT-5.6 predecessor and now matches Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 at a much lower price. On a separate software-engineering benchmark, DeepSWE, Sol scored within roughly one percentage point of Fable 5's best result while costing about 80% less per task.Factuality — long a weak point for large language models — also improved meaningfully. Based on OpenAI's internal evaluation using real conversations where users had previously flagged mistakes, Sol now makes roughly half as many factual errors as its predecessor, approaching Astra-level reliability at a fraction of the cost.* Sol: Advanced reasoning, multi‑step task automation, and integration with scientific and enterprise workflows.* Luna: Lightweight deployment, optimized for consumer applications, and faster performance on smaller devices.* Shared Advances: Improved multilingual support, adaptive memory, and enhanced contextual understanding across domains.GPT-6 Sol and Luna are rolling out today in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users, while Free and Go users can access Luna through the desktop app. Neither model is yet available in standard Chat. Developers can access both through the OpenAI API as gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna. OpenAI said the rollout within ChatGPT will happen gradually throughout the day to keep the service stable.

Luna, is a lighter and more adaptive model which is built for everyday use cases. Both the new models are created with openai’s latest alignment techniques.

Article Title: Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 is faster, cheaper and matches Fable 5.1 on most work
Article Text:
Anthropic's new Claude Opus 5.5 is 40% cheaper than Opus 5

Claude Opus 5.5 pricing undercuts Opus 5 on every token

Opus 5.5 leads benchmarks in coding and knowledge work

Anthropic adds Fable-level safeguards for biology and cybersecurity

Anthropic has launched Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in its new Claude 5.5 family, and the biggest change is cost. The company says the new AI model performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5. It also generates output more than 30% faster than its predecessor.This is Anthropic's first release since it called for pacing the AI frontier, so safety features sit right next to performance. Opus 5.5 was tested before launch by external evaluators, including METR and Frontier Design. Anthropic says it scored the best of any model on its automated behavioural audit, which runs nearly 2,000 simulated scenarios. The model is available now on the Claude Platform as claude-opus-5-5, and on Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.Input tokens cost $4 (about Rs 350) per million and output tokens $20 (about Rs 1,760), both 20% lower than Opus 5. Cache reads, which Anthropic says make up most of the bill in agentic and coding work, drop 60% to $0.20 (about Rs 18) per million. Opus 5.5 also uses fewer tokens per task, which is where the overall 40% saving comes from.Subscribers benefit too. Anthropic is raising five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans. Users also get a rate limit reset they can save and use whenever they choose.On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Opus 5.5 scored 66.4%, ahead of Fable 5.1 at 55.8% and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at 57.9%. On GDPval-AA v2.1, which tests real-world work across 44 occupations, it posted 1846 Elo against 1708 for Opus 5.Anthropic also shared results from actual workloads. One early tester completed a 680,000-line code migration in under a day. In an internal test, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 both rewrote HAProxy, a widely used load balancer, from C into Rust. Opus 5.5 finished in 9.5 hours against 12 and cost 51% less.The company says the model writes more clearly as well. It puts key information first and avoids jargon, which responds to a common complaint about Opus 5.Opus 5.5 matches Claude Mythos 5.1 in biology and cybersecurity, so it ships with safeguards similar to those on Fable 5.1. Developers can still find and fix bugs in their own code, but most cybersecurity tasks will be rerouted to Opus 4.8. Vetted labs, startups and pharmaceutical firms can apply to a new Life Sciences Verification Program. Verified security practitioners will get access through an expanded Cyber Verification Program in the coming weeks.Anthropic acknowledges some limits. It says Opus 5.5 often suspects it is being evaluated, which makes its real-world behaviour harder to predict. The company is pairing its alignment work with these safeguards for that reason.Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 are due in the coming weeks. For now, Anthropic's cheapest Opus in a generation is also the one it rates safest, even though its own tests may not catch everything.
Article Summary: Claude opus 5.5 is 40% cheaper than its predecessor. Anthropic says it performs at the level of claude fable 5.1 on most work. It also generates output more than 30% faster than its predecessors. The model is available now on the claude platform.

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple has spent several months exploring the category and is now building prototypes of a band that drops the display entirely.The early hardware pairs a thin fabric strap with a small computing module packed with sensors. Apple hasn't decided whether the product will ship. The project sits in an internal stage called a "technology investigation," and even if it moves ahead, a launch before 2028 looks unlikely. Apple declined to comment.The idea has backing from the top. Gurman reports that executive chairman Tim Cook and services chief Eddy Cue have taken a keen interest. Cue took over Apple's health teams late last year and has pushed them to borrow from newer rivals built around simpler interfaces. Engineers from Apple's Vision hardware group, the team behind Vision Pro, have also worked on the tracker.Markets noticed. Garmin, which sells display-free bands of its own, saw its shares fall as much as 2.5% after the report, while Apple stock rose about 1%.Apple remains one of the biggest smartwatch sellers, especially in the US.But Whoop and Oura have each built user bases in the millions by offering focused health tracking without apps or notifications. Oura filed for its IPO this month and is looking to raise up to $2.2 billion, while Whoop has said a listing is on the table. Google has entered the space too, with the Fitbit Air.Apple has already started borrowing from this crowd. The Apple Watch Series 12 and the revamped Health app bring a daily readiness score, more advanced heart rate tracking and an estimate of biological age. Whoop and Oura users will find all three familiar.The work also comes during a leadership change in Apple's health division. Former COO Jeff Williams retired at the end of last year, while Apple Watch marketing lead Stan Ng and fitness chief Jay Blahnik have both left.A screenless band would give Apple something it currently lacks: a way to sell its health tracking to people who don't want a smartwatch, including those unwilling to give up a mechanical watch. Before that, Apple is expected to launch smart glasses and camera-equipped AirPods in 2027, with a redesigned Apple Watch due as early as late 2027.
Article Summary: Apple is developing a screenless fitness tracker to take on whoop and oura. The company is building prototypes of a band that drops the display entirely. The project sits in an internal stage called a "technology investigation" apple hasn't decided whether the product will ship before 2028.

Article Title: Xbox lays off 268 more employees across Halo Studios and other first-party studios; company says: This brings us roughly three-quarters of...
Article Text:
Xbox is now three-quarters of the way through its 3,200-job restructuring

Activision will build the next Halo game with a new team

Xbox is merging Forza studios and moving Obsidian under Bethesda

Ninja Theory faces closure after two failed sale deals

Microsoft is cutting another 268 jobs at Xbox, and the latest round lands hardest on the studio behind its most famous franchise. Halo Studios, formerly 343 Industries, is losing staff alongside other first-party teams and the Xbox Game Studios management and central functions layer. In the same move, the next mainline Halo game is being handed to Activision, the Call of Duty publisher.Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty announced the cuts in a memo to employees. They count towards the 3,200 role reductions that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced in July for Microsoft's 2027 financial year, which ends in June 2027. About 1,600 of those jobs went in the first round. "The actions completed since July, inclusive of the studio divestitures, bring us roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring," Booty wrote.Activision is setting up a purpose-built Halo team, kept separate from its Call of Duty development. A small group at Halo Studios will stay on to support the community and the games already in players' hands. The shift comes just months after Halo: Campaign Evolved launched.Activision is also taking charge of World's Edge, the Age of Empires studio, and Rare, the developer of Sea of Thieves. Activision president Rob Kostich said the aim is to "make the greatest Halo game ever."Booty says the goal is to run fewer business units and bring together groups that already work closely. Bethesda now oversees Obsidian, which continues work on Grounded and a new Fallout project made with Bethesda Game Studios. King, the Candy Crush maker, absorbs Microsoft Casual Games, home to Solitaire and Minesweeper.Playground Games and Turn 10 Studios, partners on Forza for over a decade, will now operate as one studio handling both Forza and Fable.The plan to offload studios has had mixed results. Compulsion Games and Double Fine went independent in August with their IP, back catalogues and runway funding. Undead Labs has now followed on similar terms and, with a new publisher, will still release State of Decay 3 on Game Pass on day one.Ninja Theory, the Hellblade developer, was not as lucky. Two separate agreements to sell the studio fell through, so Xbox will begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while exploring other paths. Talks over Arkane's future in France are expected to run until the end of the year.The reason behind all of this was laid out in Sharma's July memo. Xbox was operating at margins three to 10 times lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses, and in a typical year lost 64 cents for every dollar it invested in studios. Employees will gather at an October 6 town hall, where Booty plans to look ahead to what he calls one of the strongest game lineups in Xbox history. With a quarter of the cuts still to come, that lineup now carries the weight of the reset.
Article Summary: Halo studios, formerly 343 industries, is losing staff. Activision is setting up a purpose-built halo team, kept separate from its call of duty development. Xbox is now three-quarters of the way through its 3,200-job restructuring.

Article Title: Marc Benioff says because of Microsoft, Salesforce could not invest in OpenAI; Salesforce CEO says: I knew Sam Altman very well, I was like...
Article Text:
Microsoft kept Salesforce out of OpenAI

Microsoft's 27% OpenAI stake kept Salesforce off the cap table

Salesforce's $50 million Anthropic investment from 2023 is now worth around $5 billion

Anthropic's Claude now runs Salesforce's Slack and Agentforce

Benioff lost out on OpenAI but never cut ties with it

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff wanted a stake in OpenAI long before most of the tech industry was chasing one. Sam Altman turned him down, and Microsoft was the reason. Speaking on Alex Heath's Sources podcast, in an episode published on Tuesday, Benioff said OpenAI's ties to Microsoft, a direct rival to Salesforce in enterprise software, kept the door shut.So Salesforce went to OpenAI's biggest rival instead. That fallback, Anthropic, is now valued at $965 billion and preparing for a public listing. Benioff believes the bet could earn Salesforce "not just billions but maybe tens of billions of dollars.""I knew Sam Altman very well," Benioff said on the Sources podcast. "I was like, 'Hey, I'd really like to be investing now in the company.'" According to Benioff, Altman replied that the Microsoft relationship meant Salesforce was not allowed to invest.On paper, the block made sense. Microsoft owns roughly 27% of OpenAI, uses its models in products that compete with Salesforce's, and sells OpenAI access through Azure. The two companies have reworked their deal twice since October 2025. The latest revision, in April, made Microsoft's licence to OpenAI technology non-exclusive and allowed OpenAI to serve customers on other clouds.Benioff did not claim foresight. "We felt like, whoa, we can't go here, we're going to have to go everywhere else," he told Heath, adding that it was "not because we were so smart.""Everywhere else" meant a wide spread of AI startups, including Hugging Face.Salesforce first joined an Anthropic funding round in early 2023 with about $50 million and kept investing in later rounds. By June this year, that stake was reportedly worth around $5 billion, a figure calculated after Anthropic's $65 billion raise. Salesforce has never disclosed exactly how much of the Claude maker it owns.An Anthropic IPO would put a public price on that holding and eventually give Salesforce a way to sell shares. Anthropic has confidentially filed draft paperwork with regulators, with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs reportedly leading the offering. Altman, meanwhile, has said OpenAI will not go public in 2026."It's because we have been pushed so close with Anthropic," Benioff said on the podcast, explaining why he expects such large returns.The investment has become a working partnership. Claude is the default model across Slack and runs Slackbot, which Salesforce says has saved its employees 8.1 million hours of work on an annualised basis. In August, the two companies launched Claudeforce, which brings Salesforce data into Claude through a plugin with 37 prebuilt sales skills, from meeting prep to pipeline reviews. Claude also serves as a reasoning model inside Agentforce.Money moves the other way too. In May, Benioff said Salesforce would likely spend $300 million on Anthropic tokens this year, much of it on coding.The Anthropic tie-up has not made Salesforce a one-model company. Both Dario Amodei and Altman appeared at Dreamforce 2026 in San Francisco last week, and Salesforce is adding OpenAI capabilities to Missionforce, its AI agent platform for government customers.Benioff used the same stage to call the so-called SaaSpocalypse "crazy nonsense" and to forecast that Salesforce would cross $50 billion in annual revenue next year.Three years after Altman said no, Salesforce holds an early stake in one of the world's most valuable AI companies and still has OpenAI in the room. For a company that was shut out, it ended up with a seat at both tables.
Article Summary: Microsoft's 27% openai stake kept salesforce off the cap table. Salesforce's $50 million anthropic investment from 2023 is now worth around $5 billion. Anthropic's claude now runs salesforce's slack and agentforce.

Article Title: Your AI shopping assistant could empty your account, top banks warn; says AI agents may …
Article Text:
What the banks are worried about

What the banks want to see happen

Proposed safeguards

Major banks around the world including NatWest, Bank of America, ING, Capital One, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, and New Zealand’s ASB Bank have issued a joint warning that AI-powered shopping bots could expose consumers to scams, fraud, and data-privacy breaches, as reported by Reuters. The warning from the banks comes as tech giants like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta are increasingly promoting AI agents as shopping tools, whereas retailers race to influence chatbot recommendations. As per the Reuters report, British retailer John Lewis reported that searches originating from AI agents jumped to 2.5% this year, up from just 0.3% a year ago. "They are concerned that AI agents may buy the wrong thing or spend too much – or even worse, lose their money to scams and fraud. They are not sure whether they will be protected or who they will need to go to if things ⁠go wrong," said Bank of America.In a new report, the banking coalition acknowledged that customers are genuinely enthusiastic about the potential of AI-driven shopping and eager to adopt it. But the report was equally clear that adoption is outpacing both industry standards and consumer protections, leaving a meaningful trust gap between what AI agents promise and what safeguards currently exist.The report noted that consumers remain unsure whether AI will actually act in their best interests, worrying that AI agents could buy the wrong item, overspend, or — in the worst case — lose their money to scams and fraud altogether, with little clarity on whether they'd be protected or who to turn to if something goes wrong.Specific risks flagged in the report include AI agents requesting and directly entering customers' card details into websites without adequate oversight, as well as agents potentially steering shoppers toward payment methods that offer weaker fraud protections than more secure alternatives.The coalition plans to bring a set of proposals to policymakers, including mandatory disclosure whenever an AI agent is involved in a transaction, greater transparency into how these agents actually make purchasing decisions, and stronger safeguards around customer data protection.The report also argued that both consumers and merchants should retain the freedom to choose which AI-powered e-commerce services they use, and called for different AI shopping systems to be interoperable with one another — rather than locking users into a single ecosystem's tools.To mitigate risks, banks plan to discuss proposals with policymakers, including:* Mandatory disclosure when an AI agent is involved in a transaction.* Greater transparency on how AI agents make decisions.* Stronger safeguards to protect customer data.* Ensuring consumers and merchants can freely choose which AI-powered services to use.* Interoperability across different AI commerce systems.
Article Summary: Major banks around the world have issued a joint warning that ai-powered shopping bots could expose consumers to scams, fraud, and data-privacy breaches. The warning comes as tech giants like openai, anthropic, google and meta are increasingly promoting ai agents as shopping tools.

Article Title: Boat launches smart earbuds range with Crest AI; offers Airdopes Prime 800 D, Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Nirvana Ion ANC earbuds
Article Text:
Boat launches smart earbuds range with CREST AI

Boat has launched its first smart audio devices range featuring Boat Crest AI, its AI-powered platform built with Google Gemini. The lineup includes Boat Airdopes Prime 800, Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. With the launch, Boat is introducing a new proposition for personal audio — ‘Intelligent Ears’ — earbuds designed not just for listening, but to listen, understand, converse and assist.In a press release, the company said that the Crest AI is built around a simpler idea: bringing intelligence to something consumers already wear throughout their day — their earbuds. At the heart of the experience are three capabilities — Crest Ask, G- Assist and Crest Translate, or simply: Ask. Assist. Translate.With Crest Ask, users can ask questions, explore ideas, learn and have natural conversations with AI. Instead of repeatedly reaching for a phone or typing a query, users can ask follow-up questions and continue the conversation through their earbuds.With G- Assist take the experience from conversation to action. With integration across Google Gmail, Tasks, and Calendar, users can access everyday productivity and communication capabilities through voice.From asking the assistant to “summarize my day” to “reply to an email,” G-Assist helps users manage tasks, stay on top of schedules, and interact with their digital routines without reaching for their phones.Crest Translate enables real-time, two-way translation across 25+ languages, helping people speaking different languages communicate more naturally.Gaurav Nayyar, CEO, Boat said “Why should intelligence be limited to our rooms, desks, pockets or screens? We believe it can become much more natural and simply be with you. With Crest AI, built with Google Gemini, we are bringing that intelligence to your ears. Our idea of ‘Intelligent Ears’ is simple: earbuds that can listen, understand, converse and assist. But this is just the beginning, we are working on multiple other use cases. For ten years, Boat has helped India listen. Now, we want to help India listen, understand, converse and assist”.The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D combines Crest AI capabilities with Dolby Audio and 11mm dynamic drivers tuned to Boat Signature Sound. The earbuds offer up to 45 hours of total playback, Multipoint Connectivity and four microphones with AI-ENx technology, bringing together entertainment, communication and intelligent assistance in one device.Crest AI is also available on the Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D, Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC are available through the Boat website and leading e-commerce platforms.
Article Summary: Boat launches smart earbuds range with crest ai platform built with google gemini. The lineup includes boat airdopes prime 800 and boat nirvana ion anc. With the launch, boat is introducing a new proposition for personal audio — ‘intelligent ears’

Article Title: Motorola showcases Signature 27 with 50MP main camera and 200MP periscope telephoto camera
Article Text:
Motorola launches Signature 27 with 50MP main camera and 200MP periscope telephoto camera

Motorola Signature 27 features

Motorola Signature 27 operating system

Motorola has showcased the Signature 27, its second smartphone in the Signature series and one of the first phones announced with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. The smartphone was unveiled at the Snapdragon Summit 2026 on Tuesday and comes with a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera and a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. Motorola is also changing its naming system with this phone, using the final two digits of the upcoming year for its new generations. The company has not yet announced the price or exact sale date, but says the Signature 27 will launch globally later this year.The Motorola Signature 27 is powered by Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor. Motorola says the chipset brings improvements to on-device AI, camera performance, gaming response and download speeds. The phone also comes with Motorola’s ArcticMesh cooling system. It combines diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal and copper mesh with a redesigned 3D vapour chamber. Motorola says the new vapour chamber is 40% larger than the previous generation.Motorola Signature 27 gets a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera along with a 200MP periscope telephoto camera.Motorola has also introduced its Video Enhancement Engine, which uses AI to study a scene before and during video recording and adjust colour tones in real time.The phone will also support Google's Gemini Omni, which can use prompts, photos or existing video clips to create a finished video. Google's Lyria can be used to generate music and soundtracks.The phone will be available in Pantone Coal Smoke and Pantone Capulet Green. The Coal Smoke version has a woven texture designed to improve grip and durability, while Capulet Green gets a brushed, textile-inspired finish.Motorola says the Signature 27 will receive seven years of OS upgrades and is expected to launch with Android 17. It is also the company's first smartphone with Audio by B&O, with the branding etched onto the rear panel.Motorola has not yet revealed the phone's display, battery capacity, charging speed, RAM, storage or other camera sensors. Pricing and the exact launch date are also yet to be announced.
Article Summary: Motorola launches signature 27 with 50mp main camera and 200mp periscope telephoto camera. Motorola is also changing its naming system with this phone, using the final two digits of the upcoming year for its new generations. The company has not yet announced the price or exact sale date, but says the signature 27 will launch globally later this year.

Article Title: Portronics launches Mopcop Duo, a 3-in-1 cordless cleaning device
Article Text: Portronics has expanded its product portfolio in India with the launch of Mopcop Duo, a 3-in-1 cordless cleaning device designed to make everyday cleaning more convenient and efficient. MopCop Duo combines a vacuum cleaner, air blower, and floor mop in one compact device, offering a practical cleaning solution for homes and on-the-go use.The Mopcop Duo features a sleek white finish and a compact, lightweight design that makes it easy to carry, operate, and store. Its ergonomic build lets users move seamlessly between different cleaning needs, making it suitable for everyday household use and quick clean-ups on the go.Portronics Mopcop Duo is powered by a high-performance brushless motor that delivers up to 17,000Pa of suction, helping remove dust, crumbs, pet hair, and other everyday debris. The device offers two cleaning speed modes, indicated by Tiffany Blue and White LED lights, allowing users to select the appropriate level of cleaning performance. It runs on three 2000mAh rechargeable batteries, delivering up to 30 minutes of runtime for convenient cordless cleaning.Beyond vacuuming, the Mopcop Duo is equipped with air-blowing and floor-mopping capabilities, extending its utility across different cleaning tasks. The detachable 90° flexible mop rod provides added flexibility while cleaning and mopping floors. The blower is equipped with wide-to-narrow nozzles to accommodate different air-blowing requirements. Users can easily switch between the different modes depending on the surface or task at hand.For improved dust capture and easy maintenance, the device comes with a dual-layer washable HEPA filter designed to capture fine dust particles. A 90ml dust cup helps collect everyday debris, while a range of attachments enhances its usability across different spaces. These include a narrow vacuum nozzle for corners and tight spaces and an extended hose that provides additional reach for hard-to-access areas. The Mopcop Duo can be used across surfaces and spaces including floors, sofas, cars, computers, and other difficult-to-reach areas.Mopcop Duo supports Type-C charging, making it easy to recharge using compatible charging sources.Portronics Mopcop Duo has an MRP of Rs 6,999 and is currently listed at Rs 4,099 on Portronics.com. The product comes with a 1-year warranty and can also be purchased from Amazon.in, Flipkart.com, and other leading online and offline retail stores across India.
Article Summary: Portronics mopcop duo combines a vacuum cleaner, air blower, and floor mop in one compact device. It is powered by a high-performance brushless motor that delivers up to 17,000pa of suction, helping remove dust, crumbs, pet hair, and other everyday debris. The device offers two cleaning speed modes, indicated by tiffany blue and white led lights.
